title: Clothes
subtitle: a shirt, a pair of jeans, put your coat on
summary: Name the clothes people wear every day, use the plural words like trousers and jeans, and say what someone is wearing or carrying.

lesson.heading: Clothes
lesson.text: These are the words for everyday **clothes**. Some are for work, some are for the weekend, and some keep you warm. A **sweater** and a **jumper** are the same thing.

examples.text: Joe has a job interview, so he is wearing a **suit**, a white **shirt** and a **tie**.
It's the weekend, so Julia is wearing a **T-shirt** and **shorts**.
It's cold today. I'll wear my **jacket** and take my **coat** too.

lesson.heading: Clothes words
rows: Clothes for work or a party
a suit, a shirt, a tie, a dress, a skirt
a T-shirt, a sweater (or jumper), jeans, shorts
a coat, a jacket, a scarf, gloves, boots
a watch, a ring, a belt, a hat
lesson.note: **Trainers** are sports shoes. You wear them to run or to play tennis.

lesson.heading: Plural words
lesson.text: Some clothes words are always plural in English. They need a plural verb: **trousers**, **jeans**, **shorts**, **tights**, **glasses**, **sunglasses** and **pyjamas**. You cannot say *a trouser*.

examples.text: My suit is new but these **trousers are** old.

lesson.note: To talk about one, say **a pair of**: a pair of trousers, a pair of shorts, a pair of glasses.

lesson.heading: wear or carry?

left.label: wear (on your body)
left.text: Clothes and glasses are on your body, so you **wear** them.
examples: Naomi is **wearing** a long blue coat.
Lucy is **wearing** white socks and trainers.

right.label: carry (in your hand)
right.text: Bags and other things are in your hand, so you **carry** them.
examples: She's **carrying** a suitcase and a handbag.
Gianni is **carrying** a bag with his papers and laptop.
You **carry** a bag and an umbrella.

lesson.note: You can also say **has got ... on**: Naomi has got a blue coat on.

lesson.heading: Getting dressed
lesson.text: In the morning you **get dressed** or you **put your clothes on**. At night you **get undressed** or you **take your clothes off**.

examples.text: I **put on** my socks, and then I **put on** my shoes.
He came home and **took off** his tie.

lesson.text: You **put** clothes **on** but you **take** them **off** - not ~~put your clothes off~~.
Say the words to yourself while you dress: *Now I'm putting on my socks. Now I'm putting on my shoes.*

exercises.prompt: Joe has a job interview today, so he's wearing a smart suit, a white shirt and a ___.
exercises.hint: (you wear it round your neck with a shirt)
exercises.explanation: A tie goes with a shirt when you dress smartly.

exercises.prompt: Julia's not working today, so she's wearing a T-shirt and ___.
exercises.explanation: Shorts is always plural: a pair of shorts.

exercises.prompt: Lucy is going to play tennis. She's wearing white socks and ___.
exercises.explanation: Trainers are the shoes you wear for sport.

exercises.prompt: My trousers are too big. I have to wear a ___.
exercises.explanation: A belt holds your trousers up.

exercises.prompt: Match the thing you wear with the part of the body.
Gianni is going to a business meeting. He's ___ a bag with his papers and laptop.
exercises.explanation: You wear clothes but you carry things in your hand.

exercises.prompt: Meena has got a red coat on and she ___ some flowers.
exercises.explanation: Flowers are in her hand, so she is carrying them.

exercises.statement: My favourite pyjamas is dark green.
exercises.explanation: My favourite pyjamas are dark green. Pyjamas is a plural word and needs a plural verb.

exercises.prompt: Last year Harry's trousers were white. Now they ___ grey.
exercises.explanation: Trousers is plural, so the verb is are.

exercises.prompt: Which clothes words are always plural?
You are in a shop. Ask about some jeans.
exercises.answer: Is this a new pair of jeans?
exercises.explanation: Use a pair of with plural clothes words.

exercises.prompt: In the morning you get dressed, or you ___ your clothes on.
exercises.explanation: put your clothes on = get dressed.

exercises.prompt: At night you get undressed, or you ___ your clothes off.
exercises.explanation: You put clothes on but you take them off.
